title: Bulk + loyalty discounts: two features, one shared registry
description: Type C (fake parallelism). The two features look independent ('bulk discount' vs 'loyalty program') and tempt a plan into two parallel tasks. But both land in the same shared mutable artifact (the default rule registry in shop/discounts.py), and the loyalty rule also pulls in the tier context (shop/loyalty.py). Parallel tasks that both own discounts.py collide; the honest structure is one rule-addition closure (both rules, one shared context) plus an e2e/composition test, with the engine's composition behavior (multiply all, round once at the end) frozen as a behavior contract.

anchors.description: pricing engine and its composition/rounding behavior (frozen)
Rule interface and the shared default rule registry (the collision point)
tier lookup context used by the loyalty rule predicate

must_freeze.note: engine composition behavior (all matching rules multiplicative, rounded to cents exactly once at the end) is frozen; new rules must slot into it without changing existing totals
the Rule interface (name/factor/predicate) plus the registry list is the shared contract both features extend; the tier lookup API is part of the loyalty rule's contract

must_have_edges.note: the loyalty rule predicate consumes the tier lookup API

forbidden_parallel_pairs.note: a bulk-rule task and a loyalty-rule task that both own the registry in parallel collide on shop/discounts.py; serialize them or merge them into one rule-addition closure

context_clusters.note: both rules + the tier context form one small closure

expected.notes: Type C probe: does the plan notice that 'two features' is a lie at the file-ownership level? The registry is one mutable list — parallel writers collide. Watch for: two parallel rule tasks both owning discounts.py (forbidden pair), a missing freeze of the round-once behavior, and invented scope (payments, tax, a promo framework).
